resource.name: aws_secretsmanager_secret_version
resource.description: Provides a resource to manage AWS Secrets Manager secret version including its secret value. To manage secret metadata, see the aws_secretsmanager_secret resource. If the AWSCURRENT staging label is present on this version during resource deletion, that label cannot be removed and will be skipped to prevent errors when fully deleting the secret. That label will leave this secret version active even after the resource is deleted from Terraform unless the secret itself is deleted. Move the AWSCURRENT staging label before or after deleting this resource from Terraform to fully trigger version deprecation if necessary. Write-Only argument secret_string_wo is available to use in place of secret_string. Write-Only argumentss are supported in HashiCorp Terraform 1.11.0 and later. Learn more.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` Terraform resource enables the management of individual secret versions and their values within AWS Secrets Manager, supporting secure storage and lifecycle control of sensitive data like API keys, passwords, and tokens. Common use cases include rotating secrets, maintaining version history, and ensuring controlled access to updated credentials in applications or services. Key configurations include write-only secret value management (`secret_string_wo`), handling staging labels like `AWSCURRENT` for version activation, and facilitating secret deprecation workflows to align with security best practices.

examples.title: Simple String Value
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to create an AWS Secrets Manager secret version with a simple string value using the `secret_string` argument, linking it to an existing secret via the `secret_id` attribute. This example is ideal for users looking to securely store and manage plaintext secrets in AWS."

examples.title: Key-Value Pairs
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure the `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` resource to store key-value pairs as a JSON-encoded string in AWS Secrets Manager. It highlights the use of a `map(string)` variable to dynamically define secret data and the `secret_string` argument for encoding and storing the data securely.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument represents the unique identifier of the specific version of a secret within AWS Secrets Manager. While not required, it is typically used to reference or manage a particular secret version, enabling users to track, retrieve, or interact with that version programmatically in their infrastructure configurations.

arguments.name: secret_binary
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies binary data that you want to encrypt and store in this version of the secret. This is required if `secret_string` or `secret_string_wo` is not set. Needs to be encoded to base64.
arguments.llm_summary: The `secret_binary` argument in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` resource allows users to specify binary data, encoded in base64, to be securely encrypted and stored as part of a secret's version. This enables the storage of non-textual sensitive information, such as certificates or binary files, ensuring secure access and versioning for applications or systems requiring such data.

arguments.name: secret_id
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies the secret to which you want to add a new version. You can specify either the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or the friendly name of the secret. The secret must already exist.
arguments.llm_summary: The `secret_id` argument in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` resource specifies the existing secret to which a new version will be added, using either its Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or friendly name. By defining this required identifier, users ensure the new secret version is associated with the correct secret, enabling version management for sensitive data like credentials or API keys.

arguments.name: secret_string
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies text data that you want to encrypt and store in this version of the secret. This is required if `secret_binary` or `secret_string_wo` is not set.
arguments.llm_summary: The `secret_string` argument in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` resource allows users to define plaintext data to be securely encrypted and stored as part of a specific version of a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. This enables users to manage sensitive information, such as API keys or environment variables, in a human-readable format while ensuring its confidentiality and version control within the secret lifecycle.

arguments.name: secret_string_wo
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies text data that you want to encrypt and store in this version of the secret. This is required if `secret_binary` or `secret_string` is not set.
arguments.llm_summary: The `secret_string_wo` argument in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` resource allows users to define plaintext data to be encrypted and stored as part of a specific version of a secret. It provides an alternative to `secret_binary` or `secret_string` for securely managing sensitive information, such as environment variables or configuration values, ensuring flexibility in how secrets are stored and retrieved.

arguments.name: secret_string_wo_version
arguments.description: - (Optional) Used together with `secret_string_wo` to trigger an update. Increment this value when an update to `secret_string_wo` is required.
arguments.llm_summary: The `secret_string_wo_version` argument in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` resource allows users to define a numeric value that triggers updates to the `secret_string_wo` when incremented. This argument is typically used to manage versioning or force updates to the secret's content, ensuring changes are applied even if the secret string itself remains unchanged.

arguments.name: version_stages
arguments.description: (Optional) Specifies a list of staging labels that are attached to this version of the secret. A staging label must be unique to a single version of the secret. If you specify a staging label that's already associated with a different version of the same secret then that staging label is automatically removed from the other version and attached to this version. If you do not specify a value, then AWS Secrets Manager automatically moves the staging label `AWSCURRENT` to this new version on creation. If version_stages is configured, you must include the AWSCURRENT staging label if this secret version is the only version or if the label is currently present on this secret version, otherwise Terraform will show a perpetual difference.
arguments.llm_summary: The `version_stages` argument in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` resource allows users to define a set of staging labels for a specific version of a secret, enabling precise control over version management and lifecycle transitions. By configuring this argument, users can manage the association of labels like `AWSCURRENT` to ensure proper versioning and avoid conflicts, supporting workflows such as environment-specific secret rotation or staged deployments.

attributes.name: version_id
attributes.description: The unique identifier of the version of the secret.
